packet.claim: The primary article reports 39 correct classifications out of 44 held-out Adélie individuals, approximately 88.64%, under its stated sex-classification procedure.

documents.text: Gorman, Williams and Fraser (2014), PLOS ONE 9:e 90081, DOI10.1371/journal.pone.0090081, and Palmer LTER dataset excerpts. Adult penguins were sampled at nests near Palmer Station during 2007–2009; raw Stage values are Adult, 1 Egg Stage. Body Mass (g), Species, Sex, Island and studyName are recorded fields. This is an observational breeding-season sample. Missing values are NA. The paper states body mass results are relevant to the egg-laying period and should not be considered representative of chick rearing or outside the breeding season.
documents.title: Palmer observational sampling and measurement context

documents.text: Gorman etal.(2014) Results, Sex classification, states: "all supported models accurately predicted sex for 39 out of 44 individuals (88.64%, Table 1)" for Adélie penguins at probability threshold 0.50. Methods states that structural-size models were developed using a randomly chosen two-thirds subset and assessed on a one-third subset not included in developing the models. Reported denominators are 44 Adélie, 18 chinstrap and 38 gentoo; the outcome is classification of sex in the study population, not disease, survival or clinical efficacy. Excerpt numerals are normalized with spacing; see archived primary article for the exact typography.
